items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We had dinner another time with Arvell Shaw and his wife, Madeleine who is also Swiss.

ctx.x: Kirby was engaged to play a month in a place called 'Burton's Lounges' and Burton's was one of the two clubs run by Negroes in Oakland. For one week, Buster Bailey and I got together on the Kirby book which I must admit was one of the toughest that I ever had to tackle. One of the thughest numbers I ever played was the arrangement of "Whitman Stomp" by Charlie Dickson, the Fletcher Henderson banjo player. But most of the numbers in Kirby's book were arranged by Charlie Shavers and Charlie was as touch an arranger…

We played a matinee every afternoon from five to seven, and from ten till two a.m. every night. There were plenty of sailors in town, because there was a naval base near Oakland. So the town and the joints were jumping. The prostitutes were getting rich and hinkty. Even those that looked like Wolephant had their asses on their shoulders. Wolephant is the name Arvell Shaw, the bass player, called ugly chicks, a mixture of wolf and elephant.

Kirby had a contract at Burton's for only one month, so when our time was up, he had not received another contract but promised us that he would have work for us in a few days because his agent was working on a deal. It came through - Kirby told us that the band had a gig in some town about fifty miles from Oakland.
